# Asset contract (models, animations, textures, sounds)

Single source of truth for asset names shared between the Java code and the
generator scripts in `tools/assets/`. **Do not rename anything here without
updating the Java side** (`ModBlocks`, `ModSounds`, `Anims`, `ModelBones`).

* Mod id / namespace: `squidgame`
* Minecraft 1.21.1 (Mojang mappings), Fabric, **GeckoLib 4.9.3** (classic
  `GeoEntity` + `AnimationController` API).
* Resources root: `src/main/resources/assets/squidgame/`
* Everything is **generated by Python scripts** under `tools/assets/` (Python 3.11,
  Pillow and numpy installed; `ffmpeg` with libvorbis available). Generated files are
  committed; scripts must be re-runnable and deterministic (fixed RNG seeds).
* Style: grounded recreation of the show's look - muted, slightly desaturated,
  clean pixel art. Original work only; no copying of copyrighted images or audio.

Reference material on disk (read-only, outside the repo):

| What | Path |
|------|------|
| Vanilla textures/models (style reference, block average colours) | `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bradley09roberts-glitch-github-io/4a6d7ca0-18e4-5def-acf4-50061f55720d/scratchpad/mcassets/assets/minecraft/` |
| GeckoLib 4.9.3 sources (intermediary names; read `loading/json/**` for geo/animation schema) | `.../scratchpad/mcsrc/geckolib/software/bernie/geckolib/` |
| Decompiled Minecraft 1.21.1 (Mojang names) | `.../scratchpad/mcsrc/common`, `.../scratchpad/mcsrc/client` |

(`...` = `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bradley09roberts-glitch-github-io/4a6d7ca0-18e4-5def-acf4-50061f55720d/scratchpad`)

## 1. GeckoLib models and animations

Outputs (per model `<m>` in `contestant`, `guard`, `doll`):

* `geo/entity/<m>.geo.json` - Bedrock geometry, `format_version` `1.12.0`,
  identifier `geometry.squidgame.<m>`.
* `animations/entity/<m>.animation.json` - animation names are
  `animation.<m>.<name>` (the full string is what Java passes to `RawAnimation`).
* `textures/entity/<m>.png` (+ `textures/entity/<m>_glowmask.png` where stated; GeckoLib
  auto-detects `_glowmask`).

Geometry is authored in model pixels (1px = 1/16 block), y-up, **front = -Z (north
face)**, origin at the feet centre. Humanoids use vanilla player proportions (32px tall:
legs 12, torso 12, head 8; arms 4x12x4; body 8x12x4) because the renderer scales them
by 0.9375 to match a 1.8 block hitbox.

### 1.1 `contestant` (texture 128x128, one static texture, no runtime compositing)

Appearance variety is done in Java by **per-bone tint** and **bone visibility**, so the
bone names below are a hard contract:

| Bone | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `root` > `waist` > `body` | torso (green tracksuit jacket: teal-green with white collar/stripes, zipper) |
| `body` > `head` | empty pivot bone for the head (no cubes) |
| `head` > `head_skin` | head cube, **skin area: painted near-white greyscale shading** - Java multiplies it by the skin tone |
| `head` > `neck_skin` (child of `body` is fine) | neck cube, skin |
| `head` > `hair_buzz`, `hair_short`, `hair_parted`, `hair_curly`, `hair_long`, `hair_ponytail`, `hair_bun` | one bone per hairstyle, **greyscale** texture regions, Java tints them by hair colour and shows exactly one (or none = bald) |
| `head` > `face_0` ... `face_5` | thin decal cubes in front of the face (eyes/brows/mouth sets, e.g. neutral, narrow eyes, round eyes+thick brows, freckles, tired, stern), Java shows exactly one; texture is dark ink on transparent so no tint |
| `head` > `glasses` | optional accessory, Java may show/hide |
| `body` > `left_arm` / `right_arm` | sleeve cubes (tracksuit with stripe); children `left_hand_skin` / `right_hand_skin` (skin, greyscale, tinted) |
| `left_arm`/`right_arm` > `item_left` / `item_right` | empty anchor bones at the palm for held items (needle, marble, tin) - pivot at the palm centre |
| `waist` > `left_leg` / `right_leg` | trouser cubes with white side stripe; children `left_shoe` / `right_shoe` (white sneakers) |
| `body` > `number_chest` | **empty anchor bone**, pivot at the centre of the chest bib (front, slightly in front of the jacket, e.g. z = -2.05) |
| `body` > `number_back` | **empty anchor bone**, pivot at the centre of the back bib (z = +2.05) |

Java draws the white bib and the black digits itself at the two number anchors (3x5
pixel font, procedural quads), so the model/texture must leave that area plain green and
the two anchors must sit exactly on the chest/back surface, centred horizontally. The
bib area is **9 px wide x 5 px high** (digits 3x5 with 1px gaps -> 11 px; Java scales
to 8x4.5 px - the anchor only needs the right centre point and orientation: the quad is
drawn in the bone's local XY plane facing -Z for `number_chest` and +Z for `number_back`).

A hands-free "bone naming helper" file must also be written:
`tools/assets/models/contestant_bones.json` listing the bones by role (skin/hair/face/anchor)
so a unit test can verify the geo against the Java constants.

**Animations** (`animation.contestant.<name>`). Loop type in brackets. All animate
bone rotation/position (never scale) with easing; `animation_length` in seconds.
"Overlay" animations touch only the listed bones so GeckoLib can layer them over
locomotion; "Full" animations may touch every bone.

Locomotion (Full; played by the `locomotion` controller):
`idle` [loop 4s], `idle_nervous` [loop: fidgeting, shifting weight, looks around],
`idle_confident` [loop: hands on hips / arms folded], `walk` [loop 1.0s; reference speed
2.4 blocks/s], `run` [loop 0.6s; reference speed 6.0 blocks/s, forward lean, high knees],
`stop_skid` [once 0.5s: leaning back, arms out, feet sliding - plays when a runner halts],
`turn_left`, `turn_right` [once 0.4s: in-place turn, head leads],
`freeze_balance` [loop: frozen mid-stride balancing pose, tense, one arm out],
`freeze_stiff` [loop: rigid, holding breath, fists clenched], `sneak_walk` [loop 1.2s:
slow cautious step, crouched slightly], `jump_leap` [once 0.6s, hold last pose: airborne
tuck/stretch], `fall_loop` [loop 0.5s: flailing arms, kicking legs], `land` [once 0.35s: knees
bend, recovery].

Reactions / actions (Full unless "Overlay"):
`stumble` [once 0.9s: trips, windmills arms, recovers], `lose_balance` [once 1.2s: wide arm
windmill, slips toward the edge], `shocked` [once 1.0s: recoil, hands to face],
`cower` [loop: crouched, hands over head], `sob` [loop: shaking, hands over face],
`relieved` [once 1.8s: exhale, hands on knees, wipes brow], `celebrate` [loop 1.0s: jumping
with both arms raised], `celebrate_fist` [loop 1.0s: fist pumps], `wave` [once 1.4s,
Overlay: right arm + head], `point` [once 1.0s, hold, Overlay: right arm], `nod`
[once 0.6s, Overlay: head], `shake_head` [once 0.8s, Overlay: head], `think` [loop 3s,
Overlay: hand to chin / scratch head, head tilt], `inspect` [loop 2.5s: leans forward,
head tilting, looks down at an object], `interact` [once 0.9s: reach forward and press /
grab], `eliminated_forward` [once 1.6s, **hold last frame**: collapses forward and lies prone
on the floor - the root rotates/translates so the body lies flat at floor level],
`eliminated_backward` [same, falls onto the back], `knocked_down` [once 1.2s hold: knees
then flat].

Tug of war:
`pull_idle` [loop 1.6s: braced stance, both hands on the rope, leaning back],
`pull_heave` [once 0.5s: strong backwards heave stroke, plays on every pull],
`pull_strain` [loop 0.8s: heavy exhausted straining, shaking], `pull_slip` [once 0.8s:
feet slide, loses grip, recovers].

Dalgona:
`dalgona_sit` [loop 3s: seated on a bench (waist lowered ~6px, thighs horizontal, shins down),
hunched, one hand holding the tin, other hand with needle making tiny motions],
`dalgona_carve` [loop 2s: seated, careful precise carving with head lowered and tilted],
`dalgona_lick` [once 1.8s: seated, lifts the cookie to the mouth and licks],
`dalgona_crack` [once 0.7s: seated flinch], `dalgona_success` [once 2s: seated, lifts cookie,
exhales relief], `dalgona_fail` [once 2s hold: seated, stares at broken cookie, slumps].

Marbles:
`marble_hold` [loop 2s: right fist held forward, tense, hiding marbles],
`marble_guess` [once 1.2s: shaking head / pointing / deciding], `marble_reveal` [once 1.0s: opens
hand slowly], `marble_throw_windup` [once 0.5s hold: crouch, arm back, eyes on target],
`marble_throw_release` [once 0.5s: underhand toss with follow-through].

Glass bridge:
`bridge_step` [once 0.9s: tentative testing step with one foot], `bridge_hesitate` [loop 2.5s:
crouched on the panel, one hand out for balance, looking down], `bridge_balance` [loop
1.2s: arms out wide, careful tiny steps, slight sway].

Final game / combat:
`fight_stance` [loop 1.0s: fists up, bouncing], `punch_left`, `punch_right` [once 0.35s],
`shove` [once 0.5s: two-handed push], `block` [loop 1.0s: forearms up, hunched],
`dodge_left`, `dodge_right` [once 0.4s], `knocked_back` [once 0.6s: staggered recoil],
`sprint_attack` [loop 0.5s: head-down charging run].

Misc: `sit_idle` [loop 4s: seated on a bench], `attention` [loop 4s: standing straight, arms
at the sides, chin up - lining up for guards], `hands_up` [loop 2s: hands raised in
surrender].

Total: ~55 animations. Quality bar: appealing, readable silhouettes; walk/run cycles must
be foot-planted and symmetric (left/right offset by half a cycle); loops must start and end
on the same pose; one-shots must start from the `idle` pose so blending is smooth;
rotations in degrees with eased keyframes (`easeInOutSine`, etc.); no limb clipping through
the torso.

### 1.2 `guard` (texture 128x128)

Pink jumpsuit, black hood, black mask with a white symbol; tinted per rank in Java by
bone visibility only.

Bones: `root` > `waist` > `body` > (`head` > `hood`, `mask_circle`, `mask_triangle`,
`mask_square`), `left_arm`/`right_arm` (children `left_hand`/`right_hand`, `item_right`,
`item_left` anchors), `rifle` (child of `body`; slung/held prop, Java hides it for
unarmed ranks), `waist` > `left_leg`/`right_leg` (children `left_boot`/`right_boot`).
Square-mask managers also get `collar_black` (a black high-collar bone, toggled by Java).
Java shows exactly one mask bone per rank (circle = workers, triangle = armed soldiers,
square = managers).

Animations `animation.guard.<name>`: `idle` [loop: at ease, rifle held across the
body], `idle_alert` [loop: slow scanning left/right], `idle_rigid` [loop: parade
rest, hands behind the back], `walk` [loop 1.0s; ref speed 2.4 b/s: patrol walk with
rifle], `run` [loop 0.6s; ref 6.0 b/s], `aim` [loop: rifle shouldered and aimed],
`fire` [once 0.3s: recoil], `lower` [once 0.5s: lower rifle from aim], `turn_left`,
`turn_right` [once 0.4s], `point_forward` [once 1.0s hold: points straight ahead -
directing contestants], `point_down` [once 0.8s], `salute` [once 1.2s], `open_door` [once
1.2s: presses a keypad], `inspect` [once 2s: bends to examine a body], `carry_pose` [loop:
arms forward as if carrying a body/stretcher], `clap` [once 1.0s], `wave_on` [once 1.0s:
beckoning "come" gesture].

### 1.3 `doll` (texture 256x256, glow mask)

Giant doll, **9 blocks tall** (144 px; model authored at full size, renderer scale 1.0):
orange dress with yellow collar, white sleeves, black hair with a fringe and two bob
tails, ribbon, large round eyes, dark mechanical neck joint. Static feet on a small
plinth (no leg animation).

Bones: `root` > `base` > `body` > `head` > (`hair`, `eyes_off`, `eyes_on`,
`mouth`), `body` > `left_arm`, `right_arm`, `dress`, `neck_joint` (visible mechanical ring
that animates when the head turns). `eyes_on` = glowing red/orange eye cubes (use the
`_glowmask` texture so they glow in the dark); `eyes_off` = dark dull eyes. Java toggles
`eyes_on` / `eyes_off` visibility.

Animations `animation.doll.<name>` (orientation convention, verified in-game: at entity yaw 0 GeckoLib's renderer maps the
model's north/-Z face to world +Z, so the **rest pose faces the tree** and shows her back to the players; only the head,
`neck_joint` and `neck_ring` ever yaw): `dormant` [loop: still, eyes off, tiny sway, head yaw 0], `wake` [once 2.0s: small
shudder, head lifts, arms settle, no turn], `idle_tree` [loop 4s: **faces the tree - head yaw 0 relative to the body, back of
the head toward the field**, gentle bobbing as she "sings"], `turn_to_players` [once 1.0s: head yaw 0 -> 180 with 3-4
ratchet-like pauses and a slight overshoot, finishing facing the field; the neck joint turns at half the angle; Java stretches
the playback to match the difficulty's turn time], `idle_players` [loop 3s: head yaw about 180, rigid, tiny micro-movements],
`scan_players` [loop 2s: slow sweeps left-right of the head, 180 +-25 deg, jittery servo steps], `lock_on` [once 0.4s: sharp
snap of the head toward a point, quick], `turn_to_tree` [once 1.0s: reverse of turn_to_players, yaw 180 -> 0].

## 2. Block / item / GUI textures and block models

Outputs: `textures/block/*.png`, `textures/item/*.png`, `textures/gui/**`,
`textures/entity/rope.png`, `textures/entity/rope_flag.png`, `blockstates/*.json`,
`models/block/*.json`, `models/item/*.json`, optional `*.png.mcmeta` for animated textures.
Textures are 16x16 (blocks) unless noted, crisp pixel art, no AA, matched to vanilla's
saturation level.

### 2.1 Custom blocks (all registered by Java; asset names must match)

| Block id | Model | Notes |
|----------|-------|-------|
| `bridge_glass` | cube, translucent (Java sets the render layer) | glass-bridge panel: pale cyan-white glass, thin darker frame, faint highlights. **Safe and fragile panels are the same block** - never add a visual tell. |
| `cash_block` | cube with `cash_block_top` / `cash_block_side` | bundled banknote stack (yellow-green notes with a paper band) for the prize display |
| `monitor` | `facing` (north/south/east/west), thin casing + screen on the front | `monitor_screen.png` is **animated** (`.mcmeta`, 8 frames of faint scanlines / static / tiny moving pale shapes), `monitor_case.png` dark plastic |
| `panel_light_white`, `panel_light_warm`, `panel_light_pink` | cube | ceiling light panels, bright with subtle grid lines; Java sets light level 15 |
| `playground_ground` | cube, **4 random y-rotation variants** in the blockstate | sandy packed dirt of a school playground with pebbles |
| `registration_terminal` | `facing`, non-full console (about 12 px wide, 16 px tall) with a sloped screen, card slot, pink ring light | `registration_terminal_*.png` |
| `dalgona_station` | `facing`, low table 8 px high with a small round tin and a brown honeycomb cookie on it | textures `dalgona_station_*.png` |
| `invisible_wall` | empty model with only a `particle` texture | Java makes it `RenderShape.INVISIBLE` |
| `tile_pink`, `tile_white`, `tile_black` | cube | glossy square floor tiles with thin grout (guard corridors, control room) |
| `pastel_pink`, `pastel_mint`, `pastel_yellow`, `pastel_sky`, `pastel_lilac`, `pastel_peach`, `pastel_cream` | cube | pastel stairway-maze material: flat matte colour with a very subtle pixel texture and a slightly lighter edge line |
| `pastel_<c>_stairs`, `pastel_<c>_slab` (for the same 7 colours) | vanilla stairs / slab models (use `minecraft:block/stairs`, `inner_stairs`, `outer_stairs`, `slab`, `slab_top` parents with the pastel texture) | blockstates must be complete: all 4 facings x 3 shapes x 2 halves, slab bottom/top/double |
| `symbol_circle`, `symbol_triangle`, `symbol_square` | cube, symbol on all four sides, plain top/bottom | black ground with a white symbol outline (guards' door markers) |

Items: `marble` (glass bead, a swirl of colour; `textures/item/marble.png`, model
`item/generated`), `recruiter_card` (white-bordered card with a circle, triangle, square
in red/pink; `item/generated`), plus block-item models parenting the matching block models
for every block above.

### 2.2 Entity textures (non-Geo)

* `textures/entity/rope.png` - 16x16 tileable twisted natural-fibre rope (tan/brown), the
  strands visibly twist along the **vertical** axis of the image.
* `textures/entity/rope_flag.png` - 16x16 red ribbon/flag.
* `textures/entity/player_tracksuit.png` - **64x64** vanilla-player-layout overlay
  (same UV layout as a Steve skin: head 0,0; body 16,16; right arm 40,16; right leg 0,16;
  left arm 32,48; left leg 16,48; second layer rows for jacket/sleeves/trousers), green
  tracksuit jacket + trousers with white stripes and white sneakers, **transparent
  elsewhere** so the skin shows through (head area fully transparent). Also provide
  `player_tracksuit_slim.png` (3 px wide arms, Alex layout).

### 2.3 GUI / HUD textures (`textures/gui/hud/*.png`, 16x16 unless noted, white-ish line
icons with transparent backgrounds so Java can tint them)

`icon_survivors.png` (three small people silhouettes), `icon_timer.png`, `icon_stamina.png`
(lightning), `icon_marble.png`, `icon_lick.png` (tongue/lollipop), `icon_skull.png`
(elimination), `icon_warning.png` (triangle with !), `icon_eye_red.png`,
`icon_eye_green.png`, `icon_heart.png`, `icon_rope.png`, `icon_glass.png`,
`icon_circle.png`, `icon_triangle.png`, `icon_square.png`; `number_plate.png` (32x16 white bib
with a thin border); `vignette_red.png` (256x256 radial gradient: transparent centre,
opaque-ish red edges; white-ish alpha so Java can tint); `panel.png` (48x48 nine-slice
translucent dark panel with a thin pink border, slice size 4 px).

`textures/gui/dalgona/` : `cookie.png` (128x128 honey-brown dalgona disc: mottled caramel
colours with tiny air bubbles, soft rim; **no shape drawn on it**), `table.png` (64x64 tileable
worn wooden tabletop), `needle.png` (16x32 thin metal needle with a wooden handle, tip at the

crack overlays of increasing severity).

`textures/gui/marbles/` : `hand_closed.png`, `hand_open.png` (48x48), `marble_big.png` (16x16
glass marble with highlight), `ring_target.png` (128x128 top-down target of 5 concentric
rings, red/white/blue, centre = bullseye).

### 2.4 Language fragments

Write `tools/assets/lang/textures.json` containing every `block.squidgame.<id>` and
`item.squidgame.<id>` display name (nice English names). A merge script
(`tools/merge_lang.py`, owned by the integrator) builds `lang/en_us.json`.

## 3. Sounds

Outputs: `sounds/<path>.ogg` (Vorbis, mono, 44.1 kHz, `-q:a 4`; encode with
`ffmpeg -c:a libvorbis`), and `sounds.json` mapping event ids to files with `"subtitle"`
keys. Event ids (Java `ModSounds` registers `squidgame:<id>` for each):

| Event id | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `doll.syllable_1` ... `doll.syllable_10` | the ten syllables of the doll's chant ("mu" "gung" "hwa" "kko" "chi" "pi" "eot" "seum" "ni" "da"), each 0.25-0.45 s, formant/vocoder-style sweet-creepy child-doll voice on a simple musical contour (original melody: rising then falling, last syllable lands low and held 0.6 s); loudness-matched, dry |
| `doll.turn_servo` | 1.0 s motorised neck rotation with three ratchet clicks |
| `doll.lock_on` | 0.4 s sharp servo snap + tiny chirp |
| `doll.eyes_on` | 0.7 s rising electrical hum with a crackle |
| `doll.eyes_off` | 0.5 s falling hum |
| `doll.scan_beep` | 0.3 s sci-fi scanner blip |
| `announce.chime` | 1.6 s soft three-note PA chime (descending major triad, bell tone) |
| `announce.chime_alert` | 1.2 s two-note urgent PA chime |
| `game.start_horn` | 1.5 s low brassy horn blast |
| `game.end_buzzer` | 1.2 s harsh buzzer |
| `game.win_fanfare` | 3.0 s warm victorious original fanfare (not a known tune) |
| `game.results_sting` | 2.0 s tense low string-like swell and sting |
| `countdown.tick` | 0.15 s woody tick |
| `countdown.beep` | 0.25 s clean beep, 880 Hz |
| `countdown.final` | 0.6 s higher long beep, 1320 Hz |
| `elimination.crack` | 0.5 s punchy stylised crack: noise burst + low thump (no real gunshot) |
| `elimination.buzzer` | 0.9 s descending alarm |
| `elimination.body_fall` | 0.4 s soft thud and cloth |
| `door.slide_open` / `door.slide_close` | 1.2 s pneumatic sliding door, hiss + servo |
| `door.lock` | 0.4 s heavy clunk |
| `glass.crack` | 0.7 s glass creak/crackle |
| `glass.shatter` | 1.0 s large pane shattering |
| `rope.creak` | 0.8 s taut rope creak |
| `rope.strain` | 1.2 s heavy groaning strain |
| `marble.click` | 0.2 s glass-on-glass click |
| `marble.drop` | 0.3 s small hard bounce |
| `marble.roll` | 1.0 s rolling on dirt |
| `needle.scratch` | 0.3 s fine scratching on brittle sugar |
| `dalgona.crack` | 0.4 s sharp brittle candy crack |
| `dalgona.snap` | 0.6 s cookie breaking |
| `danger.heartbeat` | 1.0 s one heartbeat (lub-dub) |
| `danger.sting` | 0.8 s dissonant stab |
| `ui.select` | 0.15 s UI click |
| `ui.confirm` | 0.4 s positive two-note blip |
| `ui.deny` | 0.3 s negative buzz |
| `ui.number_call` | 0.6 s pleasant ping when a contestant number is called |
| `ambient.dorm` | 20 s loop: low room tone, distant footsteps, faint PA hiss (no melody) |
| `ambient.playground` | 20 s loop: light wind, distant birds |
| `ambient.industrial` | 20 s loop: low machinery hum, drips, echo |
| `ambient.alley` | 20 s loop: night crickets, distant dog, faint wind |
| `music.lobby` | ~60 s loop: slow, slightly unsettling music-box + soft pad, original |
| `music.tension` | ~45 s loop: pulsing low strings synth, original |
| `music.final` | ~60 s loop: slow dramatic build, original |

Keep peak levels around -3 dBFS, no clipping, short fades to avoid clicks, loops must be
seamless (equal-power crossfade of the tail into the head).
